brewing.notes: A safe starting point for ripe pu-erh: rinse once or twice, boiling water.

description:
A ripe pu-erh from Yunnan sold under the name Cha Huang, which means tea emperor.

Treat it as you would any ripe pu-erh: rinse it, use boiling water, and let a young cake air out if it smells of the fermentation pile.
processing: Typical of ripe pu-erh: mao cha is piled, kept damp and fermented for weeks, then dried and often pressed.
harvest_season: Made from mao cha of various pickings; the season matters less than the fermentation.
appearance_dry: Usually dark brown leaf, loose or pressed.
taste_profile: Expect what ripe pu-erh usually gives: smooth, earthy and sweet.
vintage_note: Ripe pu-erh is sold by production year, usually drunk at 1 to 10 years; the first year or two often still carries a fermentation smell.
